text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The government has approved a new equity structure of the developer of the Bakun hydro-electric dam in Sarawak state. It will result in power utility Tenaga Nasional's stake in the project being reduced to five percent from 25 percent.

-- Nearly 7.4 million tourists arrived in Malaysia in 1995, compared to 7.2 million in 1994, according to the Malaysian Tourism Board. The increase was attributed to Malaysia's economic growth and stability.
-- The government is working on establishing disposal sites for radioactive waste materials that arise as by-products of mining and oil exploration activities.
-- The Bakun hydro-electric project's developer, Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd, a subsidiary of Ekran Bhd has been approved for listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange by the Malaysian government.
